name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
Open seat removes incumbency but not structural advantage
model.rationale: The D+21 lean and a heavily funded Democratic nominee against a Republican with no reported fundraising make this a Safe Democratic seat. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, and no evidence suggests a competitive general election.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Clark would be the first sign of a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open suburban Atlanta seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Georgia, with a partisan lean of D+21. Everton Blair is not on the ballot, but the Democratic nominee, Jasmine Clark, enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised over $1.6 million and drawn more than $4 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports no fundraising on record.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-20s.
